rows.name: TEST_FPGA_RESULT
rows.read_by: The step `Require successful dependencies` of job `test` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`)
rows.values: Text. The step sets it from the expression `needs.test-fpga.result`, the result of job `test-fpga`. Only the exact text `success` passes.
rows.default: Unset: the `test` command compares an empty text with `success`. The step fails.
rows.effect: The step runs `test "$TEST_FPGA_RESULT" = success`. Any other value fails the step.
rows.notes: The same step checks `BUILD_RESULT` and `TEST_HOST_RESULT` in the same way.

rows.name: TEST_HOST_RESULT
rows.read_by: The step `Require successful dependencies` of job `test` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`)
rows.values: Text. The step sets it from the expression `needs.test-host.result`, the result of job `test-host`. Only the exact text `success` passes.

rows.effect: The step runs `test "$TEST_HOST_RESULT" = success`. Any other value fails the step.

rows.name: TEST_RUNTIME_STORE_PATH
rows.values: Path of the test runtime (the Nix build output that the CI test jobs run). After symbolic links are resolved, it must have the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`.
rows.default: Unset: `publish_lab.py` stops with a `KeyError`. `prepare_handoff.py` requires the option `--test-runtime` instead.
rows.effect: `prepare_handoff.py` writes the resolved path as the output `test_runtime_store_path`. It also checks if the tests of this runtime already passed. `publish_lab.py` passes the path to `nix-instantiate` as the argument `testRuntime`.
rows.notes: In `prepare_handoff.py`, the option `--test-runtime` overrides the variable. A path of another form gives the error `invalid canonical Nix store path`. Job `tron-build` sets the variable for 2 steps: first to the build result link, then to the output of the handoff step.

rows.name: TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE
rows.read_by: The step `Validate refresh invocation` of job `plan` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`). It passes the value to `bench-refresh-ci.sh` (`bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`).
rows.values: Empty, or digits only: a whole number from `60` to `5400` seconds. Job `plan` takes it from the workflow input `measurement_timeout_seconds`.
rows.default: Unset: `bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` receives an empty argument. It skips the timeout check.
rows.effect: `bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` checks the value. A non-empty value passes only when the event is `workflow_dispatch` and the dry-run state is `true`. A value outside the range fails the step.
rows.notes: This variable only validates the input. Job `refresh` reads the same input as `SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. That variable sets the timeout of the Slice cost measurement.

evidence.quote: echo "measurement timeout override must be between 60 and 5400 seconds" \
echo "measurement timeout override requires a dispatched dry run" >&2

rows.name: TRACE_INPUTS
rows.who_sets: `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`. The step `Import structural inputs` appends the variable to the `GITHUB_ENV` file (the file that sets variables for the later steps of a job).
rows.read_by: The step `Export model traces` of job `build-model-traces` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Nix store path of the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`. `nix/model-traces-entry.nix` asserts this form.
rows.default: Unset: `nix build` receives an empty `traceInputs` argument. The assertion in `nix/model-traces-entry.nix` fails.
rows.effect: The step passes the value to `nix build` as the argument `traceInputs`. The build exports the model traces (the Torch traces of the selected models) from the files under this path.
rows.notes: The step `Import structural inputs` adds the prepared input files to the Nix store with `nix store add`. The variable holds the store path that this command prints.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_CACHE_ROOT
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/test_benchmark_runtime.py`, for a test. No workflow sets it.
rows.values: Absolute path of a directory. The helper `ci-shared-nfs.sh ensure-dir` rejects a relative path and a symbolic link.
rows.effect: `run_benchmark.sh` (the CI benchmark script) keeps each result here as `benchmark.<result identity>.json`. When that regular file exists, the script copies it to the result path. It does not measure again.
rows.notes: The option `--force` removes the cached file and measures again. The result identity is a SHA-256 hash of the payload identity, the source hash, the machine class and the host identity. `ci-shared-nfs.sh ensure-dir` creates the directory and sets its mode to `777`.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_ENVIRONMENT
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/benchmark_runtime.py`, `bin/ci/tron-build/test_benchmark_runtime.py`. The `prepare` command of `benchmark_runtime.py` appends the variable to the `GITHUB_ENV` file (the file that sets variables for the later steps of a job).
rows.read_by: `run_benchmark.sh` (`bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh`). The step `Install torch export dependencies` of job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`).
rows.values: Path of the benchmark environment (the Nix store path that holds the benchmark tools `bin/uv` and `bin/python3`). The readers use the text as given.
rows.default: Unset: `run_benchmark.sh` prints `TRON_BENCHMARK_ENVIRONMENT is required` and stops. An empty value gives the same result.
rows.effect: `run_benchmark.sh` takes its default Python from `<value>/bin/python3`. The workflow step runs `<value>/bin/uv sync` with `<value>/bin/python3` for the directory `ingest/export`.
rows.notes: `run_benchmark.sh` requires the variable even when `TRON_BENCHMARK_PYTHON` is set. `benchmark_runtime.py prepare` checks that `bin/uv` and `bin/python3` are executable files. It writes the value after this check.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_HOST_IDENTITY
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/test_benchmark_runtime.py`, for a test. No workflow sets it.
rows.values: Any non-empty text. The script uses it in a file name and as one input of a hash.
rows.default: Unset: the output of the `hostname` command.
rows.effect: `run_benchmark.sh` names the result file `<git sha7>.<host identity>.json`. The text is also one input of the result identity (the hash that names the cached result file).
rows.notes: After a measurement, `run_benchmark.sh` copies `<git sha7>.<host identity>.json` to the cache. `benchmark_save.py` writes the measurement to a file that it names with `socket.gethostname()`. `benchmark_save.py` does not read this variable.

evidence.quote: shard_id = socket.gethostname()  # one shard per machine

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_PAYLOAD_IDENTITY
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/benchmark_runtime.py`. Its `prepare` command appends the variable to the `GITHUB_ENV` file (the file that sets variables for the later steps of a job).
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. `benchmark_runtime.py prepare` writes it for the later steps of job `benchmark`.
rows.values: 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters. It is the SHA-256 hash of 2 Nix store paths: the benchmark runtime and the benchmark environment.
rows.default: Unset: nothing changes. No program reads the variable.
rows.effect: No program in the repository reads it. The later steps of job `benchmark` have it in their environment.
rows.notes: The step `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` uses a different variable, `BENCHMARK_PAYLOAD_IDENTITY`. That variable comes from an output of job `tron-build`. `benchmark_runtime.py prepare` stops when that value differs from the hash of the 2 paths.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_PYTHON
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/test_benchmark_runtime.py`, for a test. No workflow sets it.
rows.values: Path or command name of a Python program. The script runs the text as a command.
rows.effect: `run_benchmark.sh` runs `benchmark_runtime.py result-identity` and `benchmark_save.py --grid --prebuilt` with this Python program.
rows.notes: `run_benchmark.sh` still requires `TRON_BENCHMARK_ENVIRONMENT` when this variable is set.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_RESULTS_ROOT
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/test_benchmark_runtime.py`, for a test. No workflow sets it.
rows.values: Absolute path of a directory. The helper `ci-shared-nfs.sh ensure-dir` rejects a relative path and a symbolic link.
rows.effect: The result file of `run_benchmark.sh` is `<value>/<git sha7>.<host identity>.json`. The script exports the same directory as `TRON_BENCHMARK_DIR` for `benchmark_save.py`.
rows.notes: `generate_benchmark_report.sh` reads the fixed directory `/scratch/tron-benchmark`. It does not read this variable. `ci-shared-nfs.sh ensure-dir` creates the directory and sets its mode to `777`.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_RUNTIME_LIBRARY_PATH
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/benchmark_runtime.py`. Its `prepare` command appends the variable to the `GITHUB_ENV` file (the file that sets variables for the later steps of a job).
rows.read_by: The step `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` of job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Directories joined with `:`. They are the workspace directories of the files that the manifest `gen/ci-benchmark-manifest.json` of the benchmark runtime lists.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. `benchmark_runtime.py prepare` writes the variable in an earlier step of the same job.
rows.effect: The step copies the value into `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. `run_benchmark.sh` and the programs that it starts run with this library path.
rows.notes: `benchmark_runtime.py prepare` does not write `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` itself. Only this 1 step copies the value into `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

rows.name: TRON_BUILD_ARTIFACT_ROOT
rows.read_by: `ci-bundle-test-artifact.sh`, `ci-resolve-test-artifact.sh`, `ci-restore-test-artifact.sh`, `prepare_handoff.py`, and steps of `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` (`bin/ci/ci-bundle-test-artifact.sh`, `bin/ci/ci-resolve-test-artifact.sh`, `bin/ci/ci-restore-test-artifact.sh` and 2 more files)
rows.values: Path of a directory. The readers use the text as given. `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` sets `/scratch/tron-build`.
rows.default: Unset: the 4 scripts use `/scratch/tron-build`. Empty: the 3 shell scripts use `/scratch/tron-build`. `prepare_handoff.py` uses the current directory.
rows.effect: The 3 shell scripts publish, select and restore test artifact archives under `<root>/<sha7>`. `prepare_handoff.py` and `test_runtime.py` use the markers of passed tests under `<root>/<source hash>`.
rows.notes: In `prepare_handoff.py`, the option `--sentinel-root` overrides the variable. `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` passes the value as an argument to `ci-cleanup-build-artifacts.sh` and to `test_runtime.py`. `ci-bundle-artifact.sh` and `ci-run-benchmark.sh` use the fixed path `/scratch/tron-build`.

rows.name: TRON_BUILD_STORE_PATH
rows.read_by: The steps that run `test_runtime.py` in jobs `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`) and in job `refresh` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`)
rows.values: Nix store path of the test runtime (the Nix build output that the CI test jobs run). The form is `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`. `test_runtime.py` rejects other text.
rows.default: Unset: `test_runtime.py` receives an empty path. It prints `invalid canonical Nix store path` and exits with status 2.
rows.effect: Each step passes the value to `test_runtime.py` as the option `--build-store-path`. The commands `prepare`, `mark-passed` and `check-passed` take it as the path of the test runtime.
rows.notes: No script reads the variable from its environment. In `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` the value is the output `test_runtime_store_path` of job `tron-build`. In `.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml` it is the output `test_runtime_store_path` of job `plan`.

rows.name: TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS
rows.values: File descriptor numbers separated by white space. Each item is parsed with `int`. An item that is not an integer raises `ValueError`.
rows.default: Unset: `build-model.py` passes no extra file descriptor to the export process.
rows.effect: `build-model.py` passes the listed file descriptors to the process that exports the model trace. Each descriptor is a lease (an open file that holds a shared lock in the CI model weights cache).
rows.notes: `prepare_tests.py` sets the variable only when it runs a command after `--`. It passes the same descriptors to that command. `build-model.py` does not read the variable when the option `--skip-export` is given.

rows.name: TRON_TEST_ENVIRONMENT
rows.who_sets: `bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py`. Its `prepare` command appends the variable to the `GITHUB_ENV` file (the file that sets variables for the later steps of a job).
rows.read_by: Steps of jobs `test-host` and `test-fpga` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`) and of job `refresh` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`)
rows.values: Nix store path of the test environment (the store path that holds `bin/uv`, `bin/python3`, `bin/tron-test-host`, `bin/tron-test-fpga` and `lib`).
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. `test_runtime.py prepare` writes the variable in an earlier step of the same job.
rows.effect: The steps run `uv`, `python3`, `tron-test-host` and `tron-test-fpga` from `<value>/bin`. Job `refresh` also appends `<value>/bin` to `PATH` for `bench-refresh-ci.sh run-measurement`.
rows.notes: `test_runtime.py prepare` checks that the 4 programs are executable files and that `lib` is a directory. It writes the value after these checks. No script reads the variable from its environment.

rows.name: UV_VERSION
rows.read_by: Steps of the 7 workflows that set it (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`, `.github/workflows/publish-deb.yml` and 4 more files)
rows.values: Version text of `uv` (the Python dependency manager). Every workflow that sets it writes `0.9.5`.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. Each workflow that uses the variable sets it.
rows.effect: The steps build the program path `/tools/uv/<UV_VERSION>/uv` or the directory `/tools/uv/<UV_VERSION>` from it. They store the program path in `UV`, or they add the directory to `PATH`.
rows.notes: `bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh` fails when the files under `.github` give different values. It reads the YAML text, not the environment. `.github/workflows/positron-dice-deb.yml` sets the variable at job level. The other 6 workflows set it at workflow level.

new_terms.definition: A file that GitHub Actions gives to each job. A step writes a line `NAME=value` to it. The later steps of the same job then have that variable in their environment.
The Nix build output that the CI test jobs run. It is one Nix store path. It holds the `gen/` tree and the file `gen/ci-test-manifest.json`.
The Nix store path that holds the tools of the CI test jobs: `bin/uv`, `bin/python3`, `bin/tron-test-host`, `bin/tron-test-fpga` and the directory `lib`.
The Nix build output that the CI benchmark job runs. It is one Nix store path. It holds `gen/runtron` and the manifest `gen/ci-benchmark-manifest.json`.
The Nix store path that holds the tools of the CI benchmark job: `bin/uv` and `bin/python3`.
The script `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh`. It runs the CI benchmarks with the prepared benchmark runtime, or it reuses a cached result.
The SHA-256 hash of the benchmark runtime path and the benchmark environment path. It has 64 hexadecimal characters.
The SHA-256 hash of the payload identity, the source hash, the machine class and the host identity. `run_benchmark.sh` names the cached result file with it.
7 hexadecimal characters that identify the tracked source files. The step `Identify source` of `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` computes them with `git ls-files` and `sha256sum`.
The empty file `<root>/<source hash>/nix-tests-<identity>.passed`. `test_runtime.py mark-passed` creates it after the tests of one test runtime and one test environment pass.
The Torch traces of the selected models, in one bundle. The job `build-model-traces` of `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` builds them with `nix/model-traces-entry.nix`.

An open file descriptor that holds a shared lock on one lock file of the CI model weights cache. The lock files are under `state/locks` in the weights root. The cache cleanup takes the same lock exclusively.

notes: Source choices for the editor to confirm. (1) TRACE_INPUTS, TRON_BENCHMARK_ENVIRONMENT, TRON_BENCHMARK_PAYLOAD_IDENTITY, TRON_BENCHMARK_RUNTIME_LIBRARY_PATH and TRON_TEST_ENVIRONMENT are not `env:` entries. A step appends each of them to the GITHUB_ENV file. The later steps of the same job read them. None of the 6 source values describes this case exactly. These 5 rows use `step env`. (2) TRON_BUILD_ARTIFACT_ROOT fits 2 sources. `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` sets it at workflow level. 4 scripts read it with the default `/scratch/tron-build`. `.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml` calls the 3 shell scripts and does not set it. The row uses `workflow env`. (3) TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS uses `script`. `bin/ci/ingest/prepare_tests.py` sets it for a child command. `ingest/build-model.py` reads it. No workflow names it. (4) TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE is a job-level `env:` entry. Its value is an expression. The row uses `workflow env`. Facts that the input did not hold. TRON_BENCHMARK_HOST_IDENTITY: `bin/ci/benchmark_save.py` names its result file with `socket.gethostname()`. It does not read the variable. `run_benchmark.sh` then copies the file that is named with the variable. With a value that differs from the host name, these 2 file names differ. The row states both facts. It does not state a failure. No test in the checkout covers that case. TRON_BENCHMARK_RESULTS_ROOT and TRON_BENCHMARK_CACHE_ROOT: `bin/ci/ci-shared-nfs.sh ensure-dir` requires an absolute path, rejects a symbolic link and sets the directory mode to 777. TRON_BENCHMARK_RESULTS_ROOT: `bin/ci/generate_benchmark_report.sh` reads the fixed path `/scratch/tron-benchmark`. TRON_BUILD_ARTIFACT_ROOT: with an empty value, `prepare_handoff.py` uses the current directory. argparse converts the empty default to `Path('.')`. This settles the cross-area finding. TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE: `bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` validates the value: digits only, 60 to 5400 seconds, dispatched dry run only. The input said only that the value is passed on. 2 statements rest on GitHub Actions behaviour and not on code in the checkout. First, a variable in the GITHUB_ENV file reaches the later steps of the job. Second, an unset variable expands to an empty text in a `run:` script. Evidence quotes: each quote is the full source line without its leading spaces, with 1 exception. The `nix build` line of the step `Export model traces` has 144 characters. The TRACE_INPUTS row quotes an exact piece of it. No quote contains the pipe character. For TIMEOUT_OVERRIDE the 2 condition lines contain the shell operator for OR. The row quotes the 2 error message lines that follow them.
